The company and promoter are described as complainants in counterparty fraud/recovery matters, not as convicted perpetrators. For the FY2022 GST case the company says import IGST and delivery-challan differences were reconciled; an order remains pending. Repeated notices and the gross tax demand must not be added again to net booked taxes.

Director remuneration was ₹0.48 cr annually in FY2024–FY2026. Promoter ownership is indicated to fall from 91.74% to 59.63% on fresh issuance, with no OFS. factor_audit.rationale: Repeated poor stewardship is evidenced by major historical accounting corrections, failed advances and renewed substantial related-party advances without supplies. This is a stewardship assessment, not a finding of fraud.
factor_audit.contrary_fact_or_search: The IPO is entirely fresh capital, promoters retain a majority, KK returned part of its advance, and disputed tax/recovery proceedings have management explanations. Those facts do not resolve the outstanding exposure.

gates.name: Integrity and minority protection
gates.finding: Repeated poor stewardship supports GOV3 and exclusion, but evidence does not establish promoter fraud or diversion. Related supply advances, director loans and independent recovery evidence require follow-up.
gates.clearance: Independent evidence of supply/repayment, related-party safeguards and no recurrence of unsupported capitalization/advances.

gates.name: Financial reliability
gates.finding: Auditor disagrees with material receivables provisioning; an additional provision/deferred-tax note conflicts with schedules and unchanged FY26 PAT. Latest full statutory CARO/IFC not obtained; an unmodified examination opinion is not a clean annexure conclusion.
gates.clearance: Reconcile the provision/tax note, inspect latest statutory audit/CARO/IFC and establish recoveries or adjusted financials.

gates.name: Funding and survival
gates.finding: Fresh share issuance is corroborated but current unrestricted cash, eligible capex utilization, net issue fees and loan renewal/drawing power are not reconciled against admitted liabilities. Base model has a pre-IPO shortfall even at zero cash floor. Bull pre-receipt pressure under conservative monthly ordering is not evidence of observed distress.
gates.clearance: A published post-IPO cash/use statement and a credible near-term operating/funding bridge, not private daily bank statements as a formal prerequisite.

gates.name: Tradability
gates.finding: Official lot known, but complete actual daily trading rows and exit depth are missing. No 20/60 session sample is fabricated for a seven-session listing history.
gates.clearance: Retrieve all actual sessions and assess bid/offer depth, circuit locks and feasible whole-lot participation for a stated position.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Avoid — governance; unresolved financial reliability, funding and tradability also prevent an investable recommendation. This is not a fraud allegation, a finding of actual default or an instruction to trade. Paramount Syntex is a real, long-established textile operation with improving physical utilization, but the newest financial annexures are materially more cautionary than a headline profit screen.

The central issue is not simply the stock's SME label. FY2024–FY2026 cumulative CFO of ₹2.5909 cr is only 11.81% of restated PAT. The auditor says ₹3.5414 cr aged receivables warrant full provision while management provided 5%. Related supply advances of ₹10.1946 cr had not produced purchases at the reporting date. Separate director loans add ₹1.1924 cr. Earlier expansion advances of ₹6.7920 cr were already written off in restatement. Together these are repeated capital-stewardship concerns, not generic small-cap prejudice.

The company also raised meaningful fresh capital. That is important contrary evidence, but ₹61.6771 cr is intended for machinery and is not automatically free cash available to cover taxes, working capital or distributions. A post-IPO cash/use bridge is missing. The observed secondary price reference ₹80.45 is explicitly an assumption, not an authenticated historical quote row. Ordinary returns and buy-below prices are therefore unavailable. The base counterfactual, after prefunding all cash gaps with dilutive equity, returns only 7.33%, below the 15% hurdle.

BQS raw 3.56 is capped at 3.0 because GOV=3. GQS is 4.2; IAS is NS. The name is excluded from ordinary business, growth and investable rankings. Do not equate NS with a neutral score.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Issuer: Paramount Syntex Limited; ISIN INE0TBC01014; CIN U17110MH1996PLC097972; BSE SME code 544982 and symbol PARASYNTEX. Do not substitute Paramount Dye Tec, its financials or its NSE symbol. The official 19 October interop master carries PARASYNTE$; that is an interoperability identifier, not an NSE listing. Manufacturing is in Ludhiana; registered office is in Mumbai. Financial analysis is standalone under Indian GAAP Accounting Standards applicable to this issuer's AS statements, not an invented consolidated or Ind AS lease model.

Information cutoff 20 October 2026; research performed 22 October 2026. Normally the price date would be 19 October. In this case the exact historical exchange row is not authenticated: ₹80.45 is an explicitly assumed scenario reference corroborated by dated secondary displays. The five-year economic horizon is 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, 1826 days /365.25. The 15% nominal pre-tax equity hurdle is a comparison choice, not promised return. ₹500,000 is only an illustrative position.

| Gate | Question | Status | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | Integrity and minority protection | Conditional | Repeated poor stewardship supports GOV3 and exclusion, but evidence does not establish promoter fraud or diversion. Related supply advances, director loans and independent recovery evidence require follow-up. |
| G2 | Financial reliability | Hold — unresolved | Auditor disagrees with material receivables provisioning; an additional provision/deferred-tax note conflicts with schedules and unchanged FY26 PAT. Latest full statutory CARO/IFC not obtained; an unmodified examination opinion is not a clean annexure conclusion. |
| G3 | Funding and survival | Hold — unresolved | Fresh share issuance is corroborated but current unrestricted cash, eligible capex utilization, net issue fees and loan renewal/drawing power are not reconciled against admitted liabilities. Base model has a pre-IPO shortfall even at zero cash floor. Bull pre-receipt pressure under conservative monthly ordering is not evidence of observed distress. |
| G4 | Tradability | Hold — unresolved | Official lot known, but complete actual daily trading rows and exit depth are missing. No 20/60 session sample is fabricated for a seven-session listing history. |

Confidence is high in the inspected RHP financial disclosures, not in the recoverability of their balances. The complete RHP and DRHP were obtained from public mirrors with document hashes retained; direct BSE RHP retrieval was blocked. RHP financial PDF pages 212–260, including F1–F49, were inspected rather than relying on a summary. The independent examination itself warns that statutory CARO matters not affecting restatement are not reproduced. Latest full statutory CARO/IFC remain unavailable. Older FY2023 original audit portions do not fill that gap. No gate is labelled Fail solely because a document is missing.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The thirteen canonical factors are assigned once and reused. Scores are integers 1–10 or NS; exact Decimal arithmetic, no missing-factor redistribution, and ROUND_HALF_UP one-decimal display are used. BQS contributes its unrounded final value to IAS. The framework is a disciplined heuristic, not a statistically calibrated return predictor.

| Factor | Score | Confidence | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| GOV | 3 | High | Repeated poor stewardship is evidenced by major historical accounting corrections, failed advances and renewed substantial related-party advances without supplies. This is a stewardship assessment, not a finding of fraud. |
| MOAT | 3 | Medium | Process integration and customer relationships are useful but contestable. The issuer acknowledges low barriers and price competition; no verified durable price premium or share leadership. |
| REV | 5 | Medium | Predetermined three-year comparable window: FY2023–FY2026 revenue CAGR falls in 10–15%, starting score 6. Apply one negative trajectory point for the full FY2026 slowdown to 8.55% from 21.17%; not for size or profitability. No acquisitions are identified in this standalone perimeter; nominal product revenue and physical output are the scored proxies, not a claim of constant-price organic growth. |
| DUR | 4 | Medium | An accessible regional textile customer base and expansion route exist, but concentration, limited contracts and unspecified incremental saleable capacity constrain runway visibility. Do not capitalize a headline textile TAM. |
| CAP | 5 | Medium | Mixed incremental economics. The explicit multi-year NOPAT/capital bridge is positive even at selected normalized margins, so CAP is not mechanically NS for lack of private cohorts. However, impaired historical advances, fresh unproductive related assets and inventory-led profit make the raw high incremental return unreliable as a durable rate. A 12–16% nominal capital-cost range is a comparison assumption, not measured WACC. |
| CASH | 2 | High | Persistent weak conversion across four years, ageing receivables and thin bank cash are direct adverse evidence. Latest positive CFO does not offset the ratio-of-sums record. |
| BAL | 3 | Medium | Admitted tax cash obligations exceed March cash, while working-capital renewal and unknown current IPO deployment matter. The model distinguishes a selected reserve from actual default; ordinary financeability cannot be established from a capital-allotment notice alone. |
| EXEC | 4 | Medium | Existing process utilization improved, but the originally described machinery plan was enlarged and rolled forward with no orders yet placed. Prior expansion advances failed. Execution is mixed-to-weak, not inferred from absence of promotional guidance. |
| EARN | 3 | High | FY2026 profit growth is operating in form but depends on a steep margin step-up, finished-goods capitalization and unresolved provisioning. Historical restatement and fresh share dilution sharply qualify apparent EPS compounding. |
| R | NS | Low | NS: no verified current funding bridge or authenticated historical quote row. Counterfactual rescued returns are not ordinary expected returns and cannot populate R. |
| D | NS | Low | NS for a price-specific permanent-loss assessment because current claims/cash and cutoff market value are not fully authenticated. Operational downside is nevertheless substantial and quantified in stress branches. |
| P | NS | Low | NS: the public price is an assumed scenario reference. Reverse-expectation roots are valid only under an explicitly prefunded rescue and assumed funding terms. |
| L | NS | Low | NS: actual historical turnover and depth needed for a position-sized liquidity assessment were not retrieved. Seven possible listing sessions cannot become 20 or 60 observations. |

| Score | Raw | Final | Display | Coverage | Missing bounds | Contributions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BQS | 3.56 | 3 | 3.0 | 100.00% | 3.56 to 3.56 | GOV=0.60; MOAT=0.60; REV=0.60; DUR=0.40; CAP=0.60; CASH=0.20; BAL=0.24; EXEC=0.32 |

GOV3 caps BQS at 3 even though its raw score is higher. Persistent poor cash realization triggers a GQS ceiling 5 because CASH2; its raw score is already below that cap. IAS remains NS with 25% evidence coverage and 75% missing weight, rather than a point at the middle of its bounds. The governance-adjusted upper diagnostic bound is 3, not an IAS score. A two-factor GOV/CAP sensitivity is embedded separately; it does not mechanically clear the unresolved gates.

Each factor's complete supporting facts, contrary evidence, source IDs and confidence are embedded in the canonical record and reproduced in the report audit appendix. The strongest contrary facts are positive FY2026 CFO, genuine utilization gains, fresh rather than secondary IPO proceeds and partial KK advance repayment. None is omitted to make the bear case cleaner.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Paramount Syntex was incorporated in 1996 and converted to a public company in July 2024. It processes synthetic fibres and manufactures yarn/textile products, with dyeing, spinning and related processing in two Ludhiana units. Its customer ecosystem is heavily regional. It also describes trading opportunities, so product revenue cannot be treated as wholly manufactured tonnage multiplied by a single realization.

| Product | FY24 sales | FY25 sales | FY26 sales |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acrylic/knit cloth | 12.5317 | 26.5965 | 19.6541 |
| Tow/fibre | 0.4327 | 7.5374 | 5.0853 |
| Acrylic wool yarns | 46.0608 | 58.4480 | 73.9223 |
| Polyester | 13.7877 | 3.1776 | 8.0755 |
| Nylon | 16.6503 | 3.7504 | 3.7177 |
| Acrylic waste | 3.3154 | 10.5093 | 2.1749 |
| Job work | 0.0000 | 2.3892 | 3.2008 |
| Raw wool/raw waste | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 5.8538 |
| Others | 0.0000 | 0.0100 | 0.3455 |

Acrylic wool yarn now drives roughly 60.6% of sales; acrylic/knit cloth about 16.1%. Polyester, nylon and acrylic-waste sales have moved sharply between years, while raw wool/waste contributes a new ₹5.8538 cr. The FY2025 product components total ₹112.4184 cr against the printed ₹112.4179 cr, a ₹0.0005 cr source-table difference left unreconciled rather than allocated to a product. The portfolio shift makes aggregate revenue and margin harder to interpret as pure same-product volume growth. Job work of ₹3.2008 cr is only a small portion of total sales.

Customers buy for textile/knitting applications. The economic chain is procurement and processing of fibre/material, holding inventory, converting or trading it, extending customer credit, then collecting cash. Raw material and conversion costs dominate the cost base. Consequently inventory valuation, customer credit quality, purchase advances and working-capital availability are core business economics, not peripheral balance-sheet details.

FY2026 top-ten customer share 54.81% is better than FY2024's 67.36%, but Punjab still contributes 90.64%. Top-ten supplier share 62.61% also leaves meaningful procurement dependence. No long-term customer contracts were disclosed. The report does not infer durable backlog from recurring relationships or add stages of processing together as independent saleable capacity.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The most defensible strengths are local process integration, operating experience and established buyer relationships. Improved utilization indicates these assets can support business activity. They may reduce coordination and delivery costs relative to a completely outsourced operator, but no quantified unit-cost advantage, customer switching cost or protected technology was disclosed.

The company's own discussion calls the industry fragmented, competitive on price and quality, and subject to low entry barriers. That is direct counterweight to any promotional claim that sustainability or integrated processing alone establishes a moat. Recycling orientation and certifications may help qualification; they are not proof of a persistent price premium, superior returns through a textile cycle or a dominant market share.

Customer concentration has improved, which lowers one source of fragility. However, demand is still regionally concentrated and contracts do not secure long-term volumes. Competitive intensity can force more generous payment terms or inventory availability, weakening cash economics even if the income statement grows. The FY2026 margin step-up has not yet been shown to survive either lower utilization or slower collections.

MOAT3 therefore reflects useful but easily contested capabilities. It is not a prediction of collapse. A higher score would require sustained margin/cash performance through raw-material volatility, documented customer retention/qualification barriers or evidence of lower conversion cost without relying on stretched receivables and inventory. No unsupported national market-share claim or TAM percentage is used.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The predetermined measurement window is FY2023–FY2026 because a reliable common restated five-year base was not obtained. Revenue rises from ₹81.9459 cr to ₹122.0299 cr, a three-year CAGR of 14.19%. FY2024–FY2026 CAGR is 14.69%. Five- and ten-year CAGRs and current interim growth remain unavailable. No FY2027 half-year result is invented from the IPO timing.

Annual additions are ₹10.8327 cr, ₹19.6393 cr and ₹9.6120 cr. FY2026 growth slowed to 8.55% despite PAT more than doubling. REV begins at 6 for the 10–15% CAGR band, with one negative trajectory point for a complete-year slowdown. Profit margin, IPO plans and low valuation add nothing to REV.

| Process | Installed | FY24 used | FY25 used | FY26 used |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tow dyeing | 1350 | 986 | 1095 | 1100 |
| Hank dyeing | 1260 | 820 | 1073 | 1190 |
| Fibre dyeing | 2400 | 2070 | 2047 | 2100 |
| Spinning | 1200 | 1002 | 980 | 1100 |

At unchanged capacity, spinning activity rose from 980 to 1,100 in FY2026, while hank utilization reached 94.44%. This provides a real physical cross-check. However, dyeing/spinning processes overlap, so their tonnages are not additive end-customer output. New raw-wool sales and shifting polyester/nylon/waste mix further prevent a clean aggregate volume/price decomposition.

No material acquisition added to the analyzed standalone perimeter. Nevertheless, reported nominal growth is not certified constant-price organic demand growth: trading share, raw-price effects, realizations and customer additions are not fully quantified. The scored basis is same-issuer nominal product revenue, supported by activity data, at Medium confidence. A stable, standardized cross-industry demand-growth claim would be too strong. The report does not claim share gains without a comparable industry growth denominator.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The expansion route is tangible but not yet a delivered asset: ₹61.6771 cr is proposed for machinery at existing facilities. The RHP says orders were not yet placed. Vendor quotations, foreign-currency exposure, import/installation timing and customer ramp therefore sit between fresh capital and earnings. The earlier DRHP described ₹39.208 cr deployment over FY2026/FY2027; the revised plan is larger and focused on FY2027. The record supports a changed/delayed plan, not a precise attribution of every cost increase.

Existing process utilization suggests capacity pressure in hank dyeing and spinning. But an independently usable post-expansion schedule of saleable output, commissioning dates, realization and new customer commitments was not found. Forecast growth is therefore a scenario assumption, not bottom-up management guidance. Base growth 10% in FY2027 and 15% thereafter must be earned through project execution and working capital; bull 18%/22% is especially demanding.

| From | To | ΔNOPAT | Δcapital | Incremental return |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2023 | FY2026 | 14.4525 | 36.3003 | 0.3981 |
| FY2024 | FY2026 | 10.3845 | 30.0196 | 0.3459 |
| FY2025 | FY2026 | 7.5022 | 13.6228 | 0.5507 |

The bridge uses operating EBIT×(1−25.17%) and equity+interest-bearing debt−cash. At March 2026 financing capital ₹75.6086 cr reconciles to core operating net assets ₹70.4729 cr plus related advances ₹11.3870 cr, deposits ₹0.4864 cr, deferred-tax assets ₹0.6184 cr and technology-fund interest ₹0.3178 cr, less net income-tax provision ₹7.6739 cr. Ordinary operating provisions, including gratuity, remain in core operating liabilities. Displayed asset components sum ₹0.0002 cr above reported total assets; direct component core NOA is ₹70.4731 cr versus the reported-total bridge ₹70.4729 cr. The rounding residual is retained, not forced to zero. It retains related advances in capital; writing off a bad asset does not prove the investment was never made. Reported incremental returns are high, but are not project IRRs: starting earnings were restated, FY2026 margins jumped, and recovered cash is weak. A coherent public multi-year bridge can support CAP without private project cohorts, so CAP is 5 rather than automatically NS. It is also not scored 7–8 from one high reported ROCE.

Future capital spending includes both the entire IPO project and subsequent growth capex linked to incremental sales, plus maintenance capex; terminal earnings are not allowed to grow without working capital. sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The controlling family retains a majority after an entirely fresh IPO, which is better aligned than a large exit at the offer. Director remuneration of ₹0.48 cr annually is modest relative to FY2026 profit, although much larger relative to the restated FY2024 profit. Neither retained ownership nor salary alone is enough to establish stewardship quality.

The decisive record is capital allocation and accounting treatment. The DRHP also confirms original FY2023 PAT ₹12.5616 cr became ₹0.3090 cr after, among other items, reversing ₹6.6716 cr unbilled revenue into the delivery period and expensing ₹4.9610 cr capitalized operating costs. FY2024 restatement removed ₹6.7920 cr failed business advances, ₹1.2226 cr doubtful interest income and improperly capitalized expenses. New related supply advances of ₹10.1946 cr then accumulated, without purchases against the outstanding balances at March 2026. The company's explanation is that the balances are recoverable or adjustable against future supplies. KK returned ₹3.6490 cr of ₹10.3619 cr advanced during FY2026, useful contrary evidence. It does not settle the remaining ₹6.7129 cr, Paraspin ₹3.4817 cr or separate director loans ₹1.1924 cr.

The director loans are disclosed as part of a scheme bearing 12%, rather than silently described as illegal. Current pledge/encumbrance evidence was not retrieved and is not assumed zero. Audit chronology matters: prior auditor Rajesh Mehru & Co covered FY2024; Aggarwal Pawan & Associates covered FY2025/FY2026 and restatement. No unsupported inference of a resignation dispute or mandatory rotation is made.

Management's legal responses are retained. The company/promoter pursue claims against alleged fraudulent counterparties; being a complainant or witness is not being convicted of fraud. Procedural witness warrants are not a fraud judgment. Tax authorities allege differences, while management gives reconciliation explanations. Pending matters are neither ignored nor labelled finally resolved.

Execution milestones are observable: existing spinning output 1,100 versus 980, hank utilization 94.44%, revised project ₹61.6771 cr, and no machinery orders at the RHP date. No claim is made that the new project is already commissioned. GOV3 reflects repeated poor stewardship with material unresolved exposures. G1 is Conditional rather than a proved-integrity Fail; the GOV3 cap nevertheless applies consistently.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
An industrial EV/EBITDA terminal framework is used because the operating economics are processing margins and capital-intensive working capital. A precise DCF from unreliable normalized earnings would create false confidence. ₹80.45 is an assumed scenario price; authenticated cutoff price is unavailable. At that assumption,18,399,382 shares imply ₹148.02 cr equity value and 10.67× FY2026 post-IPO earnings. A March-debt/cash EV bridge is ₹180.96 cr, but explicitly is not a current post-IPO EV. Adding hypothetical IPO cash without subtracting earmarked deployment is not permitted.

The cash model begins 31 March 2026 with ₹0.3077 cr. It uses actual calendar month-end cuts plus the assumed 8 October IPO receipt,19 October entry, each fiscal year and exact 19 October 2031 terminal. Each interval’s cash uses are prefunded before operating receipts; this conservative timing convention is separate from observed daily cash. The repayable-on-demand HUF loan ₹0.1247 cr is paid at the first monthly cut. Aditya Birla ₹1 cr November renewal and larger non-renewals are stressed, not guaranteed. Net IPO cash is split into eligible project earmark ₹61.6771 cr and assumed free proceeds ₹9.9109 cr after assumed fees ₹10.20 cr. Eligible project release funds only project capex. Base and bear also deduct an explicit ₹3.2404 cr missed-collection cash effect, rather than treating fully provisioned old receivables as certain inflows. This is a foregone receipt, not a cash write-off payment, and is not deducted again from terminal value. Depreciation includes the existing run rate plus the machinery project; no separate depreciation benefit from later maintenance/growth additions is modeled, which conservatively raises projected cash tax. Base model pays the old tax provision once, preserves recurring operating taxes/interest and maintains working capital on disclosed days-based assumptions. Existing working-capital debt is rolled, not repaid magically; no uncommitted incremental facility draw is assumed.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not simply a lower textile P/E. It is that accounting earnings overstate recoverable cash while fresh capital is committed to a much larger project. Finished goods must be sold, aged receivables collected and related advances converted into supply or cash. Failure in several of these areas could leave taxes, maintenance needs and working-capital debt competing for the small unrestricted pool.

A permanent-loss chain is plausible: weaker collection and slower inventory turnover → cash shortfall before new financing → delayed or over-budget machinery → insufficient throughput and weaker margins → low incremental returns → discounted equity issuance → lower per-share value despite more nominal revenue. Circuit/lot restrictions can make an investor unable to exit promptly; tradability is separate from accounting solvency.

The modeled bear case uses 10% EBITDA margin,95 receivable days,190 inventory days,35 payable days, no related-advance recovery and full ₹1.3133 cr contingent payment. The entire proposed project still consumes capital. No survival cash is conjured from an unverified facility limit. Even the prefunded rescue branch loses substantial value at 5× terminal EBITDA. This is a stress scenario, not a forecast of actual bankruptcy.

The single most important falsification variable is recoverable cash from customers and related counterparties, measured against audited balances and actual obligations. Contrary evidence would be verified cash collection/supply adjustment, timely tax settlement, funded project completion and subsequent results whose profit converts into cash without fresh related lending. A rising share price or a clean main opinion without annexure resolution is not equivalent evidence.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A 5× price outcome over this exact horizon requires roughly 38% annual price compounding and 10× roughly 58%, before friction. It does not follow from doubling PAT off a heavily restated base. The model solves required growth only under the base margin/multiple and a fresh prefunded rescue at each trial, including the associated working-capital and share dilution effects.

These are algebraic counterfactuals, not plausible targets by default. There is no verified post-expansion saleable-capacity schedule or contracted customer ramp to support the implied scale. Persistent margin improvement, rapid turnover and unconstrained access to funding would all need evidence. A terminal multiple expansion cannot repair poor cash realization. The company does not qualify as an evidence-backed compounder candidate under the framework because governance, moat, cash and funding criteria are not met.

Reassess after the first published post-IPO financial/utilization information and each relevant half-year result, not on an invented reporting date. A development must be material to its factor: a price change can alter valuation but cannot clear a provision conflict, while a supply repayment can improve governance/cash evidence without proving a durable moat. No monitoring, external contact or trading instruction is implied by this research plan.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Avoid — governance, with concurrent Hold — unresolved for financial reliability, funding and tradability. This overrides the ordinary BQS/IAS matrix. BQS3.0 is not evidence that every aspect of the business is worthless; it is the mandated consequence of GOV3. IAS remains NS, not “cheap,” “expensive,” or zero. GQS describes the quality of observed growth, not permission to invest.

Research priority is to resolve the audit provision inconsistency, recoverability of related assets, post-IPO unrestricted cash and actual tradeability. Merely lowering the assumed purchase price does not clear those issues. A materially improved evidence set could change the classification, but evidence of repayment must be weighed against controls and recurrence rather than treated as an automatic score reset.

For an existing holder this is a review candidate because stewardship, financial reliability and execution matter. This report cannot specify a quantity to sell, a tax-aware exit plan or a time-to-exit without portfolio context and authenticated liquidity. The user has asked for research, not trades. No order has been placed and no public recommendation is implied.

The company is not an evidence-backed compounder candidate. It is also not labelled a proven fraud or actual funding default. Keeping these distinctions explicit is more useful than either dismissing all SME issuers or accepting headline IPO growth uncritically.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary-document coverage includes the complete 2026 RHP and 2025 DRHP obtained through mirrors, with original-content hashes recorded. Source-safe extracts retain the financial facts, source URLs, page locations and calculations; they do not claim to authenticate an inaccessible original exchange payload. Full original PDFs, OCR, personal identifiers and transfer credentials are deliberately not embedded in the research package.

The decisive page map is RHP PDF212–217/F1–F6 for the examination report, PDF233–234 for receivables/cash/advances, PDF252–255/F41–F44 for restatement, PDF260/F49 for contingencies, PDF155 onward for mix, PDF164 for capacity, and PDF88 onward for machinery objects. RHP financial-indebtedness figures are March 2026 balances certified in September, not current October balances. The source ledger distinguishes those dates.

Open questions: latest full statutory audit/CARO/IFC; reconciliation of the provision/deferred-tax note; independent recovery of aged receivables and related advances; final issue fees and actual receipt/utilization; current unrestricted cash and renewal/drawing power; post-expansion output/commissioning economics; exact price/mix/trading bridge; and all actual exchange sessions with depth. Missing data stay unavailable and no third-party message or outreach was sent to obtain them.

Main assumptions are explicit in model inputs: ₹80.45 scenario price, ₹1 cr operating reserve, assumed 8 October receipt, ₹10.20 cr issue fees, renewal of existing working-capital borrowings, tax rate 25.17%, debt interest 9%, maintenance capex 1.5% of sales, further growth capex 15% of incremental sales, and no dividends. They are sensitivity variables, not newly discovered facts. Base/bear closing-cash gaps are distinguished from the bull monthly pre-receipt sequencing gap and the selected reserve.

This is financial research, not personalized investment advice. Exact model results, all 48 sensitivity rows and all annual/dated interval rows are embedded in the canonical record. Calculation reproducibility does not replace source authentication, professional audit or a realistic execution check.

FY2026 debt is ₹33.2480cr, including ₹25.4155cr working-capital loans and ₹7.8325cr term debt/current maturities. Cash ₹0.3077cr is entirely cash on hand/imprest; bank balances are zero. The company and promoter are described as complainants in counterparty fraud/recovery matters, not as convicted perpetrators. For the FY2022 GST case the company says import IGST and delivery-challan differences were reconciled; an order remains pending. Repeated notices and the gross tax demand must not be added again to net booked taxes.

The complete 2026 restatement examination and notes were read. They explicitly exclude CARO matters not affecting restated numbers; original FY2023 CARO/IFC cannot clear FY2026. Financial page F44 prints a ₹0.8897976cr provision and ₹0.5798cr deferred-tax impact, while note 16/P&L show a ₹0.1771cr FY2026 provision and the FY2026 restatement leaves PAT unchanged. This is an unresolved document inconsistency, visually checked, not an OCR correction.

₹80.45 is corroborated by dated secondary displays, but no complete historical BSE daily row was retrieved. It is therefore an assumed scenario price. Only seven post-listing weekdays existed through 19 October; 20/60-session statistics remain unavailable. Missing/pre-listing periods are not zero-volume days. A lot would cost ₹80,450 at the assumption, without implying exit liquidity.

This is a synthetic fibre/yarn, dyeing and textile-product business with trading opportunities. Management describes a fragmented market, low entry barriers and price/quality competition. No verified share leadership or persistent pricing premium supports a strong moat.

Director remuneration was ₹0.48cr annually in FY2024–FY2026. Promoter ownership is indicated to fall from 91.74% to 59.63% on fresh issuance, with no OFS. summary:
Avoid — governance; unresolved financial reliability, funding and tradability also prevent an investable recommendation. This is not a fraud allegation, a finding of actual default or an instruction to trade. Paramount Syntex is a real, long-established textile operation with improving physical utilization, but the newest financial annexures are materially more cautionary than a headline profit screen.

The central issue is not simply the stock's SME label. FY2024–FY2026 cumulative CFO of ₹2.5909 cr is only 11.81% of restated PAT. The auditor says ₹3.5414 cr aged receivables warrant full provision while management provided 5%. Related supply advances of ₹10.1946 cr had not produced purchases at the reporting date. Separate director loans add ₹1.1924 cr. Earlier expansion advances of ₹6.7920 cr were already written off in restatement. Together these are repeated capital-stewardship concerns, not generic small-cap prejudice.

The company also raised meaningful fresh capital. That is important contrary evidence, but ₹61.6771 cr is intended for machinery and is not automatically free cash available to cover taxes, working capital or distributions. A post-IPO cash/use bridge is missing. The observed secondary price reference ₹80.45 is explicitly an assumption, not an authenticated historical quote row. Ordinary returns and buy-below prices are therefore unavailable. The base counterfactual, after prefunding all cash gaps with dilutive equity, returns only 7.33%, below the 15% hurdle.

BQS raw 3.56 is capped at 3.0 because GOV=3. GQS is 4.2; IAS is NS. The name is excluded from ordinary business, growth and investable rankings. Do not equate NS with a neutral score.
